split_method: Train on32731 excluding latest file, SHA256(run:event)%5==0 and user examples33/52. Whole excluded events are same-run holdout. All32739 is cross-run holdout. No heldout target data used to fit coefficients.
method: Predict per256ns median ADC changes. Separate single-reference weighted fits from13/14/16; primary output is median of>=2 available reference predictions. Instantaneous and symmetric3tap FIR sensitivity. Reference edge20..2000ADC in training; target edges>2000 and raw rail bins excluded. Ridge0.001mean Gram diagonal. >=100 training samples in>=10 events per reference-target pair.
predictive_skill_definition: 1 - sum(observed_edge-predicted_edge)^2/sum(observed_edge^2), on observed paired samples only. Negative means worse than predicting zero. This is not a fraction of photons, physical energy or pure electrical signal.
limits: All references share AFE1; models may miss other electrical modes.
Disconnected status follows the established user/slide identification13/14/16; input11 excluded because of its distinct code-scale population.

Good prediction establishes shared predictability with unlit inputs, not the initiating source. Optical activity can induce correlated electrical pickup; regression can then also predict a real optical component.
A residual is unexplained by this model, not classified light. Poor transfer does not exclude electrical coupling.
FIR uses one future256ns bin as an offline shape test. It is not a causal predictor or an early-warning algorithm.
Self-triggered missing bins are never zero-filled; results are conditional on paired recording and>=2 usable witnesses.
Training regions are disjoint by time but all records are shake-selected; far packets may contain recovery.
Event-shuffled predictions use a different heldout event from the same raw file and split, scored on exactly shared observed samples.
Large edges and rails are censored. Cross-run differences may include configuration or operating-state changes.
No calibrated channel gains, measured circuit impedances, optical templates or photon decomposition.
